item.text: The repository currently attaches `TokensUsed` to response types, and the stream reader leaves completion text uncounted. I’ve added the new counter API and am wiring it into the agent’s request loop; the production Assist and web callers are being updated in parallel.

package model

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/sashabaranov/go-openai"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestTokenCount(t *testing.T) {
	prompt, err := NewPromptTokenCounter([]openai.ChatCompletionMessage{
		{Role: openai.ChatMessageRoleUser, Content: "hello"},
		{Role: openai.ChatMessageRoleAssistant, Content: "world"},
	})
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, 10, prompt.TokenCount()) // Two message overheads and one token per content.

	completion, err := NewSynchronousTokenCounter("hello world")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.Equal(t, 5, completion.TokenCount())

	stream, err := NewAsynchronousTokenCounter("hello")
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, stream.Add())
	require.NoError(t, stream.Add())

	count := NewTokenCount()
	count.AddPromptCounter(nil)
	count.AddCompletionCounter(nil)
	count.AddPromptCounter(prompt)
	count.AddCompletionCounter(completion)
	count.AddCompletionCounter(stream)
	gotPrompt, gotCompletion := count.CountAll()
	require.Equal(t, 10, gotPrompt)
	require.Equal(t, 11, gotCompletion)

	// Reading the usage finalizes the stream, without waiting for a producer.
	require.Equal(t, 6, stream.TokenCount())
	require.Error(t, stream.Add())
	gotPrompt, gotCompletion = count.CountAll()
	require.Equal(t, 10, gotPrompt)
	require.Equal(t, 11, gotCompletion)
}
